_meta.traceability: docs/test-plan/TC_Matrix_FR13.md; hw02_ref names the HW02 case or open question each row derives from
_meta.validated_at_runtime: automation/tests/fr13_dashboard/fr13.dashboard.spec.ts validateCases() checks this count, duplicate tc_ids, the type/layer/actor/check/final_status enums, finite seed amounts, positive integer `repeat`, non-empty integer expect_http_any_of, non-negative delta_precision and cart item shape - and throws with the full list before any test runs.
_meta.expectations_are_spec_derived: Every expect_* value states what the SPECIFICATION requires, never what this build currently does. README.md FR-13 L183 defines revenue as the sum of total_amount over status='delivered' ONLY - no multiplier. Rows that fail are findings, not values to recalibrate (project rule 4).
_meta.why_deltas_not_absolutes: The dashboard shows GLOBAL totals and the SUT database is never reset between the nine required runs, so an absolute expectation like 'revenue = 100' (as HW02 wrote them) is unrunnable here - it was only ever valid on an empty system. Each row therefore measures the CHANGE the seeded orders cause, which is invariant to whatever the database already holds.
_meta.seeding: seed_orders are created via POST /api/checkout, which takes total_amount straight from the request body with no recomputation, then walked to final_status through PUT /api/admin/orders/:id/status. Verified reachable amounts: 0, 1, 0.01, -1, -0.01, large. The walk is pending -> confirmed -> shipping -> delivered; 'canceled' is reached from pending.
_meta.account_safety: Only TC-18 sends a wrong password to the seeded admin, once per browser worker after its signed setup token already exists. Other negative-login rows use empty/unknown identities. Setup tokens are minted locally from SUT_JWT_SECRET, so worker restarts do not consume login attempts.

fields.title: becomes the Playwright test title
fields.layer: ui (assert on the admin app) | api (assert on the endpoint directly)
fields.hw02_ref: HW02 case or open question this row carries over or closes
fields.actor: admin | non_admin | anonymous | malformed_token | expired_token | signed_missing_role | signed_nonexistent_admin | non_admin_token_injected | admin_token_injected | throwaway_user
fields.credential: for login rows only: valid | wrong_password | unknown_email | empty. Keeps 'what is typed into the form' in the data instead of branching on tc_id in the spec
fields.seed_orders: orders to create before measuring, or null. amount is the client-supplied total_amount; final_status is where the order is walked to; optional `repeat` creates N copies
fields.cart_items: server-side cart contents for the recomputation case: {name, price, quantity}
fields.raw_total: deliberately malformed checkout total for API validation rows; may be null/string/object
fields.expect_recomputed_total: the exact total the backend must store, derived from cart_items
fields.delta_precision: decimal places for a delta comparison. Absent means the delta is an integer and is compared EXACTLY; present only where the UI's 3-fraction-digit rendering makes exactness impossible
fields.expect_revenue_delta: required CHANGE in the revenue KPI, per the specification
fields.expect_count_delta: required CHANGE in the order-count KPI
fields.expect_http_any_of: acceptable status codes where the requirement is 'must be refused' but the exact code is an unresolved open question
fields.expect_dashboard_rendered: whether the dashboard must be reachable for this actor
fields.expect_alert_contains: the app's own message; safe to assert because it is app-supplied, unlike FR-01's browser-native validation strings
fields.note: why the row exists / what settles the expected value

cases.title: admin reaches the dashboard and both KPI cards render a numeric value
cases.note: Baseline. Asserts both cards are visible AND parse to a finite number - 'a card exists' would pass against an empty or NaN value.

cases.title: dashboard is the landing view; no navigation is required to reach it
cases.note: Pins the routing fact that invalidated the scaffold's '/admin/dashboard' (gap analysis finding 12). If a router is ever added, this row is what notices.

cases.title: revenue KPI equals the sum of total_amount over delivered orders
cases.note: The headline assertion, recomputed from GET /api/admin/orders - the same payload the UI derived its figure from, so a mismatch cannot be blamed on a stale fetch. README FR-13 L183 is the source of the rule.

cases.title: order-count KPI equals the number of orders the API returns
cases.note: Closes OQ-02, which HW02 left open by listing 'all orders' and 'delivered only' as candidates and asserting neither. This row commits to 'all orders' and records the answer either way.

cases.title: revenue is rendered as currency, with a symbol and grouped thousands
cases.note: Closes OQ-07. Asserts the ₫ symbol and a grouped integer part. NB the grouping character comes from the browser, not the app (toLocaleString with no locale) - the assertion is on structure, not on a literal string.

cases.title: a canceled order does not enter revenue
cases.note: HW02 wrote this as 'revenue = 100' on an empty system; restated as a delta so it survives an accumulating database.

cases.title: a pending order does not enter revenue
cases.note: HW02 collapsed the three non-delivered live statuses into one case. Split here because they are three distinct equivalence classes and the exclusion logic is per-status.

cases.title: a confirmed order does not enter revenue
cases.note: See TC-06a.

cases.title: a shipping order does not enter revenue
cases.note: See TC-06a. This is the status immediately before delivered, so it is the one most likely to be included by an off-by-one in the filter.

cases.title: a delivered order of 0 changes revenue by 0
cases.note: DIAGNOSTIC ROW. 0 is the one delivered amount a doubling fault cannot distort (0*2 = 0). If this row is green while BVA-03/05/06 are red, the fault is multiplicative rather than a wrong status filter or a double-counted row - one reading instead of a wall of red.

cases.title: a delivered order of 1 increases revenue by exactly 1
cases.note: Smallest positive integer amount. The minimal input that separates 'counted once' from 'counted twice'.

cases.title: a delivered order of 0.01 increases revenue by 0.01, not by a rounded 0
cases.note: Sub-unit amount. Two separate sources of imprecision, neither of which may be widened to hide the doubling: the column stores 0.01 as 0.009999999776482582 (single-precision float, ~2e-10 error), and the UI renders through toLocaleString(), which caps at 3 fraction digits. 3 decimal places is therefore the tightest the RENDERED figure can be asserted to - not a chosen tolerance but a ceiling the display imposes. It still separates 0.01 from 0.02.

cases.title: a delivered order of -1 decreases revenue by exactly 1, not clamped to 0
cases.note: Settles OQ-16, which HW02 flagged as possibly unreachable: POST /api/checkout accepts a negative total_amount and stores it, verified. Whether a negative order SHOULD be creatable is a separate question for FR-08, not for this row.

cases.title: a delivered order of -0.01 decreases revenue by exactly 0.01
cases.note: Negative sub-unit: the corner where a sign error and a rounding error would look alike. Same 3-decimal rendering ceiling as BVA-05.

cases.title: three delivered orders 1000/2000/3000 increase revenue by exactly 6000
cases.note: Multi-row aggregation: distinguishes 'each row doubled' from 'one row counted twice', which a single-order case cannot.

cases.title: one delivered order of 0 is distinguishable from having no delivered orders
cases.note: Closes OQ-18, which HW02 left open and 'not graded either way'. Revenue alone cannot tell the two states apart; the count KPI must move even though the revenue does not.

cases.title: a canceled order must not be transitioned to delivered
cases.note: HW02's TC-13 was 'delivered -> canceled removes the amount', which cannot run: the machine has no rule for a delivered source, so it is refused with 400. Restated onto the transition that IS permitted - server.js:566 explicitly allows canceled -> delivered, which lets a cancelled sale re-enter revenue. Expected value is 'refused'; the specification lists no path back out of canceled.

cases.title: revenue is recomputed after a transition into delivered, not cached
cases.note: Carries HW02's real intent for TC-13 - re-read the dashboard AFTER a status transition, which HW02 never did. Expects the FULL amount: FR-13 L183 defines revenue over `status = 'delivered'` with no clause about how the order arrived there, so once the order IS delivered the dashboard must count it. Whether the transition should have been permitted is a separate question, and TC-13 asserts it at the API. An earlier draft expected 0 here, which wrongly encoded TC-13's rule into an FR-13 row and would have made the two cases report the same defect twice.

cases.title: the order-count KPI keeps counting past a 25-order batch
cases.note: Closes OQ-12. HW02 treated 'confirm all orders are returned' as a manual precondition. A page limit of 10, 20 or 25 would cap the delta below 25. This global KPI uses an at-least delta because another suite sharing the SUT can create an unrelated order during the 25-request seed batch; a clean Chromium run observed exactly that (FR11 order id 101 interleaved between FR13 ids 100 and 102).

cases.title: a client-supplied total_amount is recomputed by the backend, not stored as sent
cases.note: Closes OQ-06, flagged in HW02 as a concern but never tested. README FR-08 requires the backend to recompute the total from the cart; api_specification.md 4.3 lets the client supply it. The cart is filled through POST /api/cart with known prices, so the correct total is EXACTLY 150000*2 + 99000 = 399000, and the row submits 999999999 instead. Asserting the stored value equals 399000 - rather than merely differing from what was sent - is what makes this falsifiable: a build that stored any other wrong number, or clamped, would pass a not-equal check.

cases.title: a non-admin's credentials are refused at the admin login form
cases.note: The app's own string, raised via alert(); Playwright auto-dismisses dialogs unless a handler is installed, so without one this row could only observe 'still on the form' and not why.

cases.title: empty credentials are refused
cases.note: Empty string is a legitimate input, not a missing value. The form has no required attribute, so the request is actually sent.

cases.title: an unknown e-mail is refused without revealing that the account does not exist
cases.note: README FR-02 L42 requires the refusal not to disclose the cause. Same message as a wrong password, so the two are indistinguishable to a caller - which is what the requirement asks for.

cases.title: a wrong password is refused for an account that does hold the admin role
cases.note: Separates 'wrong password' from 'not an admin', which TC-04 alone cannot. Deliberately NOT run against admin@eshop.com: one failure sets login_attempts to 2 and a second locks the account for 3 minutes, which would fail every later row in the run.

cases.title: an anonymous visitor sees the login form and no KPI figures
cases.note: Asserts the revenue figure is absent, not merely that the login form is present - a dashboard rendered behind a modal would satisfy the weaker check.

cases.title: a malformed token in storage does not render the dashboard
cases.note: The app trusts localStorage on load and only clears the token if a request comes back 401/403. This row checks that recovery path works.

cases.title: a valid non-admin token in storage does not render the dashboard
cases.hw02_ref: TC-04 / BUG-08 at the UI layer
cases.note: The row TC-04 cannot reach. The admin check lives ONLY in handleLogin, so a token that never passes through the form skips it entirely; the app then calls the admin endpoints, which accept a non-admin token. TC-04 passing while this fails is the whole point - it shows the gate is cosmetic.

cases.title: logging out clears the stored token and returns to the login form
cases.note: Asserts the token is gone from storage, not just that the form reappeared - a logout that only resets React state leaves a reusable token behind.

cases.title: GET /api/admin/orders without a token is refused
cases.note: api_specification.md 6 requires a Bearer token on every admin endpoint.

cases.title: GET /api/admin/orders with a malformed token is refused
cases.note: Either code is a correct refusal; the specification does not distinguish them, so the row does not invent precision it never had.

cases.title: GET /api/admin/orders with a valid NON-ADMIN token is refused
cases.note: api_specification.md 6 L173: 'tài khoản phải có quyền Admin'. authenticateToken verifies the signature and never reads role, so authentication is being used where authorisation is required. HW02 logged this as BUG-08.

cases.title: GET /api/admin/users with a valid NON-ADMIN token is refused
cases.note: A second endpoint behind the same middleware, so a fix that only patches the orders route is still caught. This one also returns every user's e-mail address.

cases.title: GET /api/admin/orders with an admin token returns the order array
cases.note: The control row for API-01 to API-04: without it, a server that refused everyone would pass all four refusal rows.

cases.title: PUT /api/admin/orders/:id/status with a NON-ADMIN token is refused
cases.note: Extends the access-control question from reading to WRITING. If a non-admin can drive an order to delivered, they can move the revenue KPI directly. Targets an order this row seeds, so no pre-existing data is mutated.

cases.title: a user cannot grant themselves the admin role through PUT /api/users/me
cases.note: server.js:137-145 reads `role` from the request body of the self-update endpoint and writes it. If this succeeds, every other access-control row in this suite is moot: any user can become an admin and then log in through the admin form legitimately. Runs on a throwaway account, so no shared fixture is promoted.

cases.title: a mixed batch of all five statuses moves revenue by the delivered amount only
cases.note: HW02's TC-01 set-up ('5 orders, one per status') as a single atomic case, which the four separate exclusion rows cannot express: each amount is distinct, so if the wrong status leaked in, the delta identifies WHICH one by its value rather than just reporting 'not 44000'. Also the only row where inclusion and exclusion are exercised in one measurement.

cases.title: reloading the dashboard twice does not change either KPI
cases.note: Guards against a KPI that accumulates per fetch rather than being recomputed - the failure mode that would make every delta row above read correctly on the first measurement and drift on the second. Nothing is seeded, so both deltas must be exactly 0.

cases.title: a valid ADMIN token placed in storage does render the dashboard
cases.note: CONTROL ROW. Without it, TC-04b ('a non-admin token must not render the dashboard') could pass for the wrong reason - because token injection does not work at all, rather than because the role is checked. This row proves the injection mechanism itself is sound, which is what gives TC-04b's result meaning.

cases.title: an expired token is refused by the admin endpoint
cases.note: TC-03 covers a token that is structurally invalid; this covers one that is correctly signed but past its expiry, which is a different code path in jwt.verify. The token is minted by the test with an `exp` in the past. NB the SUT issues tokens with NO exp claim at all (server.js:69 calls jwt.sign with no expiresIn), so this row asserts that expiry is honoured when present - it does not claim the SUT expires its own sessions.

cases.title: the admin orders payload carries the fields the revenue KPI depends on
cases.note: Every revenue assertion in this suite reads `total_amount` and `status` off this payload, so a rename or a type change there would silently invalidate all of them. Asserts each row has a numeric id, a finite numeric total_amount and a status drawn from the five known values. This is the row that would have caught the scaffold's `order.total` mistake (gap analysis finding 15) at the contract rather than as a confusing revenue mismatch.

cases.title: a correctly signed token with no role cannot read all orders
cases.note: Separates authentication from authorization: a valid HMAC proves who signed the token, but absence of an admin role must still deny the global order feed. Catches middleware that treats jwt.verify success as admin permission.

cases.title: an admin-role token for a nonexistent user cannot read all orders
cases.note: A role claim must not be trusted without resolving an active user in the database. Uses an impossible user id with a valid signature; a 200 means deleted/nonexistent identities retain admin data access.

cases.title: GET /api/admin/users without a token is refused
cases.note: Checks route-level middleware wiring independently from /admin/orders. The payload contains every user's e-mail and lockout state, so accidental public exposure is materially different from the KPI feed.

cases.title: anonymous status update is refused without mutating the order
cases.note: Covers the no-credential branch on the revenue-moving write endpoint and asserts both the refusal code and that the seeded order remains pending.

cases.title: malformed-token status update is refused without mutating the order
cases.note: Exercises jwt.verify failure on a write route, then reads the owner's order back. This catches handlers that mutate before sending an authentication error.

cases.title: checkout rejects null total and creates no KPI source row
cases.note: FR-13 consumes order totals globally, so invalid checkout data is an upstream trust-boundary risk. The case checks both validation and absence of the side-effect row.

cases.title: checkout rejects a nonnumeric total and creates no KPI source row
cases.note: A text value can survive SQLite's INTEGER affinity and later make dashboard aggregation display NaN. It must be rejected before an order row exists.

cases.title: checkout rejects an object total without returning an internal error
cases.note: An object reaches the database binding path differently from scalar bad values. A controlled 4xx and no order distinguish input validation from an unhandled 500.

cases.title: checkout rejects a numeric string and creates no KPI source row
cases.note: Numeric-looking text often passes loose coercion while changing storage/type semantics. FR-08 requires server recomputation from the cart, not trust in any client total representation.

cases.title: order count crosses the 100-row pagination boundary
cases.note: TC-14 catches limits at 10/20/25; this crosses the common 50/100 boundaries. At-least 101 tolerates unrelated concurrent orders in the global KPI while still exposing truncation. Requires the documented LOADTEST=1 harness mode because the SUT's global 200-request limiter is lower than a complete FR-13 run.
